clue.text: Yearning to forego last tablet

indicators.note: to forego is to do without, and last says it is the final letter of the yearning word that goes

parts.note: yearning means aspiring, longing for something

explanation.surface: Someone longing for something gives up their final pill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to forego last' drops the final G of ASPIRING.
explanation.definitionFit: A common painkilling drug sold as small pressed pills, so a tablet is one example.

clue.text: Work in theatre bound to include good lines

indicators.note: to include means the word for bound takes another letter within it

parts.note: bound, as in certain to happen, means sure
RY, short for railway, stands for lines (railway tracks)

explanation.surface: An actor's stage job will surely have some fine lines to deliver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Theatre' suggests the stage, but it is the operating theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: Operations are carried out by surgeons in an operating theatre, the hospital room so named.

clue.text: It's matured and gone off? Initially, yes

definitions.text: It's matured and gone off? Initially, yes

indicators.note: Initially says to take the opening letter of each of the preceding words in turn

explanation.surface: A question about whether something has ripened and spoilt, answered with a cautious yes.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: a fully developed insect has matured and flown off.
explanation.definitionFit: The final adult stage of an insect, after it emerges and can fly away, is the mature form.

clue.text: PM once rebuffs Democrat from an ME country

indicators.note: rebuffs means turns away or rejects, so the Democrat's letter is pushed out

parts.note: Benjamin Disraeli was a Victorian British prime minister

explanation.surface: A former prime minister snubs an American Democrat.
explanation.walkthrough: ME is Middle East; the D lost is Disraeli's first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective for things or people belonging to the Jewish state on the eastern Mediterranean.

clue.text: Cat's in the bag — start to hunt bear

indicators.note: in places the cat's word inside the word for the bag

parts.note: a sac is a bag-like pouch in a body
a tom is a male cat; the 's is read as is

indicators.note: start to means the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: The cat has been bagged, and now the hunt for a bear begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bear' looks like the hunted animal but is the verb, to tolerate.
explanation.definitionFit: To be able to put up with or tolerate something, as in 'I can't stomach it'.

clue.text: Time to put out paper

parts.note: to put out a publication is to issue it

explanation.surface: It is the moment to publish the newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'paper' suggests a newspaper, which 'put out' reinforces; it is the soft thin kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Thin soft paper used for wrapping or for blowing the nose is called by this name.

clue.text: A human staggered, inhaling foul air, the dope!

indicators.note: inhaling means taking in, so the reworked air goes inside the reworked human letters
staggered means reeling, so the letters of a human are shaken up
foul means fouled or tangled, so the letters of air are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone lurches after breathing bad air and is called an idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staggered' makes MHUAN and 'foul' makes ARI, which 'inhaling' sets inside; the clue's opening A goes last. 'dope' looks like a fool but is the drug.
explanation.definitionFit: Dope is slang for cannabis, the drug smoked from the hemp plant.

clue.text: Med resort hosts international for Wolves, maybe

indicators.note: hosts means takes in as guests, so the resort's name holds the extra letter

parts.note: Cannes is a resort on the French Mediterranean coast

explanation.surface: A Riviera resort hosts an international match for Wolverhampton Wanderers football club.
explanation.walkthrough: Wolves is the nickname of Wolverhampton Wanderers, an English football club; here it is the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Wolves belong to the dog family, so they are examples of this group of animals.

clue.text: Big bottle full of hard fruit containing radical sources of energy

indicators.note: full of means the bottle holds the next letter inside it

parts.note: a carboy is a large bottle, often in a protective frame
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

indicators.note: containing means the fruit word holds the radical's letter within

parts.note: dates are the fruit of the date palm
R is an abbreviation for radical

explanation.surface: A large jar filled with tough fruit and radical ingredients makes a power supply.
explanation.definitionFit: Sugars and starches in food are broken down by the body to release energy.

clue.text: Top-class gunmen conserve energy but waste material

parts.note: U is an old label for upper-class usage

indicators.note: conserve means keep safe within, so the gunmen hold the energy letter

parts.note: RA, the Royal Artillery, is the British army's gunnery regiment
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Elite gunmen save their strength yet still produce rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: A compound excreted in urine as the body's way of getting rid of surplus nitrogen.

clue.text: Giving heart to sons at university breeding hogs

indicators.note: hogs means takes over and holds, so the breeding word engulfs the others

parts.note: rearing animals means breeding them
S is the abbreviation for son, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: Students away at college raise pigs, which cheers them up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hogs' looks like the pigs being bred, but it is the verb that encloses.
explanation.definitionFit: Encouraging or comforting someone is giving them heart, restoring their confidence.

clue.text: Zurich banker invests European cell contents

indicators.note: invests means puts money into, read as putting the next letter inside

parts.note: Swiss financiers are nicknamed the gnomes of Zurich

explanation.surface: A Swiss financier puts money into a European firm's holdings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invests' plays on banking but signals inclusion.
explanation.definitionFit: The complete set of genetic material carried within each cell of an organism.

clue.text: Groom's job? Running after bride at the start

indicators.note: after means the running word follows the bride's letter
at the start means only the opening letter of bride is used

parts.note: running means rushing, going fast

explanation.surface: A bridegroom dashes along behind his bride as the wedding begins.
explanation.walkthrough: The groom is not the bridegroom but someone who grooms horses or hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Grooming a horse or one's hair means tidying it with a bristled tool.

clue.text: Get a load of Tories to tour British plant

indicators.note: to tour means to go round, so the looking and Tories words together surround the British letter

parts.note: to get a load of something is slang for to look at it, to eye it
the Right is the political wing Tories belong to

explanation.surface: Look at the Conservatives touring a British factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' suggests a factory for Tories to visit; it is a wild flower.
explanation.definitionFit: A small meadow flower once used to treat eye complaints, a herbaceous example of flora.

clue.text: Instinctive activity to do with washing clothes

indicators.note: clothes is the verb, covering something, so the washing word wraps the next piece

parts.note: washing oneself in a tub is bathing
re means about, to do with

explanation.surface: Doing the laundry, clothes and all, as a reflex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothes' reads as laundry but is the verb, to dress or cover.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking in and letting out air happens automatically, without conscious thought.

clue.text: Units in temple belt round it perhaps

indicators.note: in places the units inside the temple word

parts.note: a wat is a Buddhist temple in Thailand or Cambodia
units are ones, written as the letter I, so two of them pluralised give IS

explanation.surface: Monks in a temple wear belts around their robes.
explanation.definitionFit: A belt is worn around the middle of the body, so the body's middle is where it goes.

clue.text: Ailsa Craig, say, has been rented

parts.note: has been is read as is, as in it has been or is now
a rented property is let

explanation.surface: A woman named Ailsa Craig has rented out a property.
explanation.walkthrough: Ailsa Craig looks like a person but is a small rocky island in the Firth of Clyde, off Scotland's west coast.
explanation.definitionFit: A small island, of which that Scottish rock in the sea is an example.

clue.text: Bone up over in opera house

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the opera house's name

parts.note: La Scala is the famous opera house in Milan

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the word up is read backwards

explanation.surface: Cram again at the opera house before the curtain falls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bone up' reads as a phrase meaning to study; 'Bone' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The shoulder blade, a flat triangular bone at the back of the shoulder.

clue.text: Daniel ran off, stimulated by this?

definitions.text: Daniel ran off, stimulated by this?

indicators.note: off means out of order or wrong, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Daniel fled, perhaps spurred on by a rush of a fight-or-flight hormone.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: someone who runs off is driven by this hormone.
explanation.definitionFit: The hormone released in fear or excitement that prepares the body to fight or flee.

clue.text: A German consumes final sort of protein

indicators.note: consumes means eats up, so the German word holds the next piece

parts.note: ein is German for a
final means last

explanation.surface: A German eats a last meal of a type of protein.
explanation.definitionFit: A stretchy structural compound in skin and arteries, one kind of protein.

clue.text: In university, English Literature's flipping pointless

indicators.note: flipping means turning over, so the English and literature letters are read backwards

parts.note: Lit is short for literature; the 's is read as is

explanation.surface: A student complains that studying English Literature at university is flipping useless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' looks like a mild British swear word but signals the reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: Useless, serving no purpose, a rare formal synonym for futile.

clue.text: Selection of poetry in Greek requiring effort

indicators.note: Selection of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Choosing from verse written in Greek is hard work.
explanation.definitionFit: Difficult or wearing, demanding hard work or patience to deal with.

clue.text: Stalin's enforcer concealed routine bugs

indicators.note: concealed means hid inside, so the enforcer's name holds the routine

parts.note: Lavrentiy Beria headed Stalin's secret police
a performer's routine is an act

explanation.surface: Stalin's police chief hid the routine of planting listening devices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bugs' suggests the spying devices of Stalin's police but means germs.
explanation.definitionFit: Bugs, informally, are germs or microbes that cause illness.

clue.text: A spruce shelters posh courtyard

indicators.note: shelters means protects within, so the spruce word holds the posh letter

parts.note: spruce means neat, smart, trim
U is an old label for upper-class, posh usage

explanation.surface: A spruce tree shades an elegant courtyard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spruce' suggests the tree but is the adjective, neat.
explanation.definitionFit: An open central court in a Roman house or a modern building's covered hall.

clue.text: Arm reinforcements organising raid to capture island

indicators.note: to capture means to hold inside, so the rearranged raid letters take in the island
organising means arranging, so the letters of raid are reordered

explanation.surface: Military reinforcements are organised to raid and seize an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organising' turns RAID into RADI; 'to capture' puts I between its D and I. 'Arm' reads as military but means the limb.
explanation.definitionFit: The forearm's supporting bones, plural of the one on the thumb side, strengthen the limb.

clue.text: Unicef works with mint, dispensing lots of money

indicators.note: works means operates on, so the letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: The children's charity teams up with the Royal Mint to hand out cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Lavishly generous, giving freely and in large amounts.

clue.text: Medic with very little cash for drug supplier

parts.note: Dr is the abbreviation for doctor, a medic
1p, one penny, a tiny sum, is read as the letters IP

explanation.surface: A doctor with hardly any money turns to dealing drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drug supplier' suggests a dealer, but it is the hospital device.
explanation.definitionFit: A bag and tube feeding medicine into a vein, so it delivers a drug to the patient.

clue.text: Book season involving censor's cases

indicators.note: involving means wrapping in, so the season word takes the censor's word inside

parts.note: a season and an age are both periods of time
a censor's gag silences speech

explanation.surface: A book for this season involves the censor's legal cases.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cases' suggests legal actions but means suitcases.
explanation.definitionFit: Luggage, the suitcases and bags taken on a journey.

clue.text: Foreign invader, colonist with current information

parts.note: an ant lives in a colony, so it is a colonist
I is the physics symbol for electric current
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: A settler arriving from abroad, carrying the latest news.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foreign invader' sounds like a colonist, but it is a substance the immune system attacks.
explanation.definitionFit: A substance alien to the body that triggers the immune system to produce antibodies.
